name: analytics-dashboard
description: The studio's deploy dashboard: a sidebar, four number tiles, a 14-day chart and a table of recent deploys, with the sidebar tucked away behind a menu button on a phone. A baseline, not a pass-or-fail test: the registry has a table and a tag but no chart, sidebar or drawer, so this records what the agent hand-builds (or installs) for the chart and for the phone navigation, and how it looks.
prompt:
The home page of this Next app is still the starter. Replace it with the studio's deploy dashboard. A sidebar on the left with the litt.design wordmark at the top, then Overview, Projects, Clients and Settings. At the top of the page, four number tiles: active projects 12, deploys this week 38, median build 41s, uptime 99.98%. Under them, deploys per day for the last 14 days as a chart, oldest first: 5, 7, 4, 9, 6, 1, 0, 6, 8, 5, 9, 7, 2, 1. Then a table of recent deploys with project, branch, status and time:

Halo site, main, ready, 2 min ago
Northwind rebrand, redesign/nav, building, 9 min ago
Atlas portfolio, main, ready, 1 hour ago
Lumen docs, fix/search, failed, 3 hours ago
Kassa pitch deck, main, ready, yesterday
Case study template, content/q4, ready, 2 days ago

On a phone the sidebar should get out of the way. Behind a menu button is fine.

This is for litt.design, our own studio site, not client work, so make the calls yourself. Make sure it builds and looks right in light and dark, and on a phone.
look:
Judge the page-* screenshots (the dashboard as loaded, light and dark, 1440 and 390 wide, full page) and the nav-phone-* screenshots (after tapping the menu button on a 390 wide touch screen). Claims:
1. page at 1440: a sidebar runs down the left edge with the litt.design wordmark and four items: Overview, Projects, Clients and Settings. Overview is marked as the current page by a fill or a color, not by bold text or a dot. The dashboard sits to the right of it.
2. page at 1440: four tiles at the top read Active projects 12, Deploys this week 38, Median build 41s and Uptime 99.98%, each with a small label. The figures stand out by size and tone and not by weight. The tiles are flat: a hairline edge and a soft fill, slightly rounded corners (about 8px), no drop shadow and no colored bar on an edge.
3. page at 1440: a chart of deploys per day shows 14 marks, one per day, in order. Their heights follow 5, 7, 4, 9, 6, 1, 0, 6, 8, 5, 9, 7, 2, 1: two peaks of 9 on the 4th and the 11th day, nothing (or the lowest mark) on the 7th day, and the last day at 1. Axis labels or value labels let a reader tell the numbers, and a title or caption says what the chart shows.
4. page: the chart is quiet. The marks use one tone (neutral or a single tint), the gridlines are thin or absent, and there is no gradient fill in or under the marks, no rainbow of colors and no shadow or glow on the marks.
5. page at 1440: the table of recent deploys has the columns Project, Branch, Status and Time and six rows, from Halo site to Case study template. Status is a small tag in a monospaced font, with slightly rounded corners (about 4px, not a pill), that says ready, building or failed in words, where only the text carries the status color, the tag's fill stays neutral and there is no dot. Rows are separated by hairlines with room around the text, and the header text is not bold.
6. page at 390: the sidebar is out of the way. No sidebar column sits beside the content, which uses the full width. A menu button is visible. The tiles stack in one or two columns, the chart fits inside the screen with no mark cut off, and the table is readable or scrolls inside its own box.
7. nav-phone: after tapping the menu button the navigation is open over the dashboard and shows Overview, Projects, Clients and Settings, in a panel, drawer or menu with a hairline edge and a soft glow or shadow with no hard offset. Its rows are tall enough to tap (about 44px), and the page behind is dimmed or the panel clearly sits above it. If the navigation is not visible, fail this claim.
8. All screenshots: all text is regular weight (nothing bold), there are no emoji, no decorative gradients and no hard offset shadows, and no large flat accent fills: the chart marks, the tiles and the sidebar are not filled with the accent color (accent text on the current item, a thin accent line or a single highlighted mark is fine). The keyboard focus outline and the one soft light from the top (litt's light source, a faint tint that fades down a surface, once per view) are allowed. In the dark screenshots the tiles, chart and table are set off from the page by a hairline and a fill at least slightly lighter than the page, and all text is legible.
